subject: Performance SLO follow-up: latency targets, throughput & cost levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps - latency SLOs and cost levers

Hi Jordan / Pauline -

Thanks for taking the call today - great to learn more about Nova Retail's chat assistant rollout. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of requirements
- Target p95 latency: <= 350ms for short queries (<= 64 tokens)
- Streaming for long-form guidance (responses > 512 tokens) with first-token latency target <= 500ms
- Expected concurrent users at peak: 450 sessions, average concurrency ~80-120
- Throughput target: ~25 qps sustained, spikes to 60 qps during promotional windows

Primary risk areas we flagged
- High concurrency patterns could push token costs if batching is suboptimal
- Streaming plus long outputs may increase GPU memory pressure and KV cache requirements

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a draft SLO matrix (Nova_SLO_matrix_20260913.xlsx) - please review and confirm the p95/p99 targets and streaming requirements.
2) If you can share a small sample of typical prompts and an anonymized traffic profile (CSV or histograms), we'll run a quick perf model to recommend batching/caching/quantization settings. Perf sample file attached as perf_sample_logs_20260913.txt.
3) Rishi will follow up with estimated cost ranges for three serving configurations (hosted low-latency, hosted with batching+cache, and dedicated with 8xA100-like capacity).

Short ask: can you confirm the p95 target (350ms) and whether streaming must start output within 500ms for long responses?

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference - production-first LLM inference

Attachments: Nova_SLO_matrix_20260913.xlsx (spreadsheet), perf_sample_logs_20260913.txt (log sample)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novaretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pauline Tran <pauline.tran@novaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - latency SLOs and cost levers

Thanks Marissa - that captures the call well. Confirming:
- p95 350ms is our goal for short queries. We can tolerate p99 up to ~900ms for long prompts if streaming is smooth.
- Streaming: yes, first-token within 500ms is important for perceived responsiveness (mobile users).
- Traffic: I attached a sample traffic_histogram.csv to a follow-up reply (will upload via Drive link if needed).

One follow-up question: how much latency uplift should we expect when enabling continuous batching vs single-request low-latency mode? We need rough numbers to present to our engineering leadership.

-Jordan
Senior PM, Nova Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - latency SLOs and cost levers

Jordan -

Great, thanks for confirming. Short answers below, and Rishi will add numbers for your traffic profile. Longer explanation and concrete tradeoffs in the attached SLO matrix.

Continuous batching vs single-request low-latency
- Batching increases per-token latency slightly for the first token (typical first-token delta ~30-120ms depending on batch size and model), but reduces overall cost per token significantly at moderate--high QPS by improving GPU utilization.
- For your p95 350ms target on short queries, we can remain within target with small batch windows (10-30ms batching delay) on hosted configs if we pin to a low-latency kernel and use prefix caching for repeated context.

Caching and KV strategies
- Prefix/KV caching will save substantial compute for repeated prompts (recommend enabling for shopping-cart/context prompts) and will also improve p95 for follow-on interactions.

Quantization & model variants
- 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants can reduce memory and increase throughput; expect 1.5-3x throughput uplift with modest quality delta for instruction-following tasks. We'll propose a model-variant test matrix (baseline FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit) in the next note.

Concrete next steps
1) Rishi: run a quick perf simulation against the traffic histogram Jordan will share and produce: a) expected p95/p99 by configuration b) estimated monthly cost for the three configs.
2) Priyom: can you slot a 90-min technical deep-dive with Nova's infra team this week to validate streaming/kvcache behavior?
3) Jordan: upload the traffic sample to the Drive link in my previous email or reply with the CSV.

I'll prioritize the SLO matrix updates and include example latency uplifts for batching windows of 0ms/10ms/30ms and quantization options.

Thanks,
Marissa

---

Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps - latency SLOs and cost levers

Jordan - looping in a few quick, back-of-envelope numbers based on similar retail workloads and the sample distribution Marissa mentioned. These are estimates; I'll run the traffic sample through our perf simulator after you upload it and send a follow-up spreadsheet.

Option A - Low-latency hosted (single-request prioritization):
- Config: FP16 model, low-latency kernel, batching disabled or 0-5ms window
- Expected p95 (short queries): ~220-320ms
- Cost: highest per-token; baseline monthly estimate: $13k-$22k for the stated traffic (depends on exact token shapes)

Option B - Hosted with small batching + KV caching:
- Config: FP16 or 8-bit hybrid, batching window 10-30ms, prefix KV cache enabled
- Expected p95: ~260-360ms (still within your 350ms target with careful tuning)
- Throughput: 1.8-2.8x efficiency vs A at steady state
- Cost: ~40-55% of Option A (depending on cache hit rate)

Option C - Dedicated reserved (higher concurrency headroom):
- Config: Dedicated GPU pool, 8-bit quantized variant available, aggressive batching when safe
- Expected p95: ~200-300ms at scale, best cost per token for sustained high throughput
- Cost: higher committed monthly but lower marginal cost for spikes

Streaming notes
- For streaming first-token latency <=500ms, prioritize low-latency kernel for first-token and then switch to chunked generation; our runtime supports a hybrid: first-token fast path + batching for subsequent tokens. This keeps perceived latency low while preserving throughput.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with example numbers once I run your CSV. Priyom - can you propose 2-3 time slots for the technical deep dive?

-rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) For Option B, is the 10-30ms batch window a configurable SLO parameter we can tune in production?
2) For quantization tests, can you include quality regression metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or our internal correctness checks) alongside latency/cost?

If yes to both, go ahead with the perf run and we'll pick a deep-dive slot after you propose times.

-Jordan
